claims.text: Donald Trump stated on October 16 that he did not request a reduction in Starshield services for Ukraine.
Elon Musk stated that any limits on speed or usage of Starshield systems were decided by the US military and ultimately the US president.
Ukraine uses SpaceX's Starshield satellite system for battlefield communications, mid-range strikes on Russian-occupied territory, and interceptor drones.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that White House officials told his partners they asked SpaceX to restore Starshield service.
Donald Trump called for Volodymyr Zelenskyy to be replaced following criticism over a US deal allowing more Russian diesel into global markets.
Volodymyr Zelenskyy asked EU leaders in Brussels to keep financing Kyiv's fight with nearly $80 billion more next year.
Donald Trump branded Kyiv's renewed strikes on Russian oil refineries a 'disgrace'.
Donald Trump stated that he finds Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy more difficult to deal with than Russian President Vladimir Putin.
European Council chief Antonio Costa stated that it is time to increase support to Ukraine and pressure on Russia.
Donald Trump struck a deal to buy Russian diesel on October 12.
EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas stated that Europe cannot replace Starlink's satellite internet capability for Ukraine in the short term.
The EU provided Ukraine with an approximate $100 billion (€90 billion) loan last year.
Starlink restricted satellite internet speed limits to 100 mph (160 km/h) on Tuesday night.
Around 600,000 people in Ukraine were left without power after communications and energy facilities were hit in missile strikes.
A bipartisan group of US senators signed a letter demanding an investigation into the disruptions to Ukraine's Starlink network.
Volodymyr Zelenskyy told the European Council that the war will cost €155 billion next year, with at least €70 billion needed from the EU.
Reuters reported that two US officials and a Western official said the order to throttle Starshield came from inside the White House.
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen stated that there is a €70 billion funding gap for Ukraine that needs to be covered for 2027.
Volodymyr Zelenskyy proposed creating an EU-controlled custodian for frozen Russian assets to manage unfreezing risks.
A 16-year-old gunman killed four people at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon, before being shot dead by an armed bystander.
The four fatalities in the Bend elementary school shooting were five-year-old Rhoam Summer, an eight-year-old child, an 11-year-old child, and 25-year-old teacher Megan Lambert.
Seven-year-old Saylor Graham and 54-year-old teacher Becky Drury were hospitalized with injuries following the shooting.
Police identified the 16-year-old gunman at Silver Rail Elementary School as Griffin J. John II.
The gunman carried out the attack using a Maverick 88 12-gauge pump-action shotgun legally purchased by his mother in August.
An armed father driving past the school pursued the gunman inside and shot him dead.
A teacher at the school confronted the gunman by throwing her phone and tackling him before he was shot.
Mourners gathered at a makeshift memorial outside an elementary school in Bend, Oregon.
US President Donald Trump called the armed bystander who shot the gunman a 'great hero'.
The National Rifle Association stated that the Oregon incident served as a reminder of the importance of an armed citizenry.
The 16-year-old suspect forced entry into the elementary school by firing at locked doors.
White House press secretary Katie Zacharia is transitioning out of her role.
US President Donald Trump told White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia to reconsider her job five days after taking office.
Katie Zacharia admitted she failed the bar exam and was not licensed to practise law in the United States, despite previously describing herself as a lawyer.
Katie Zacharia sparked controversy in an interview by stating that China does not 'even have proper toilets'.
Chinese Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning advised Katie Zacharia to 'visit China more often'.
Katie Zacharia was appointed White House press secretary on October 9 to succeed Karoline Leavitt.
Katie Zacharia's five-day stint as press secretary is shorter than Anthony Scaramucci's 10-day tenure as White House communications director.
Katie Zacharia graduated from Pepperdine University's law school in 2011.
White House Communications Director Steven Cheung described Katie Zacharia as 'uniquely qualified and whip smart'.
A White House official confirmed on October 16, 2026, that Katie Zacharia was let go from her role as press secretary.
Parents demanded accountability following a school roof collapse in Peshawar, Pakistan, that killed 34 children.
At least 33 pupils and a teacher were killed after a roof collapsed at the private Al-Khair school in Dir Colony, Peshawar.
Police arrested the owner of Al-Khair school following the roof collapse.
Peshawar police chief Mian Saeed stated that the three-story building was overloaded and built with substandard roof slabs.
Governor of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Faisal Karim Kundi ordered a safety audit of all schools in the province.
At least 45 children suffered injuries in the Al-Khair school roof collapse in Peshawar.
A total of 110 students were attending lessons across three classrooms when the roof collapsed.
Pakistan spends less than 1% of its GDP on education.
Yemeni Information Minister Moammar al-Eryani reported that Houthis fired two missiles that landed near the runway at Aden International Airport.
Yemeni military spokesman Majed al-Nazili claimed government forces neutralized over 430 Houthi fighters in Marib province within 24 hours.
Iran's Ministry of Foreign Affairs denied playing a role in Houthi operations and offered to mediate between the Houthis and Riyadh.
Former Yemeni Prime Minister Maeen Abdulmalik Saeed warned that the fall of Taiz to Houthi rebels would endanger Western security and maritime control.
Southern secessionist leader Aidarous al-Zubaidi called for a mobilization of southern troops and a referendum on secession within two years.
Five people were killed and 16 injured in a Houthi missile attack targeting al-Maashiq presidential palace in Aden.
Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree stated that their missiles struck the Saudi military operations headquarters in Aden.
Yemen's health ministry reported that at least 1,282 people have been killed in fighting in Yemen since August 6.
The UN Security Council issued a joint statement condemning escalatory Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and commercial shipping.
Riyadh's international airport has been targeted by Houthi strikes 20 times since the beginning of the month.
Saudi Arabia reported intercepting a Houthi cruise missile over Medina province.
